jobs.title: Executive Director, Ambulatory Services
jobs.description:
Grider Support Services, LLC & Premier Health Partners, PC are proud partners of Erie County Medical Center (ECMC) and are dedicated to providing high-quality patient-centered care to our community.

We are seeking an Executive Director, Ambulatory Services to provide executive leadership and strategic direction for Premier Health Partners (PHP), a multi-specialty ambulatory physician practice consisting of eight service lines and approximately 90 employees, including providers and support staff. This role is responsible for the overall strategic, operational, and financial performance of PHP and serves as a key leader in advancing growth, operational excellence, provider engagement, quality, and patient experience.

The Executive Director will partner closely with hospital and health system leadership to align PHP services with broader organizational priorities. This position provides executive oversight of strategic planning, financial performance, service-line growth, workforce leadership, physician relationships, value-based payer arrangements, innovative payment models, and initiatives designed to improve access, quality, efficiency, and patient-centered care.

The ideal candidate will be an accomplished healthcare executive with significant experience leading complex ambulatory operations, physician practices, or multispecialty healthcare organizations and a demonstrated ability to drive organizational performance and strategic growth.

Responsibilities

Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for all Premier Health Partners (PHP) practices.
Establish and execute strategic priorities, business plans, and growth initiatives that support the organization's mission and long-term objectives.
Maintain accountability for the financial and operational performance of the PHP practices, including budgeting, resource allocation, revenue cycle performance, expenses, provider productivity, patient access, and service-line performance.
Partner with hospital leadership to ensure alignment between practice operations, strategic priorities, and broader organizational objectives.
Provide leadership and direction to providers, clinical leaders, managers, and support staff, fostering accountability, engagement, collaboration, and high performance.
Partner with physician leadership to align clinical practice, operational performance, provider needs, and organizational strategy.
Manage and direct activities related to value-based payer arrangements and innovative payment models, including implementation, performance monitoring, and collaboration with payers and internal stakeholders to support organizational and financial objectives.
Oversee the development and implementation of initiatives to improve patient experience, efficiency, and service-line performance.
Identify opportunities for growth, expansion, and development of ambulatory services in alignment with organizational strategy and market needs.
Ensure compliance with applicable healthcare laws, regulations, accreditation standards, organizational policies, and quality requirements.
Serve as a senior representative of the practice and foster strong relationships with physicians, hospital and health system leadership, organizational stakeholders, community partners, and other key external partners.
Lead organizational change and continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen the practice's clinical, operational, financial, and organizational performance.

Benefits:
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package. The hiring range is between $250,000 to $300,000 per year/hour. Enjoy generous PTO, paid holidays, and top-tier medical coverage with low premiums and full deductible coverage through an HRA—plus dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) with a 3% employer match and great discounts!

Qualifications

Experience:
8-10 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare administration, physician practice management, ambulatory operations, or a multispecialty medical group.
At least 5 years in a senior management or executive leadership role with responsibility for complex operations, financial performance, strategic planning, and organizational leadership.
Education:
Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, or a related field required. Master's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, or a related field preferred.
Specialized Knowledge/Skills:
Comprehensive knowledge of ambulatory healthcare operations and physician practice management.
Expertise in strategic planning, financial management, budgeting, and operational performance.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multidisciplinary organizations and engage physicians, clinical leaders, and support staff.
Knowledge of healthcare quality, regulatory compliance, patient experience, and continuous improvement.
Exceptional executive-level communication, relationship management, negotiation, and decision-making skills.

Applicants and employees are considered for positions and are evaluated without regard to mental or physical disability, race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, genetic information, military or veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other protected Federal, State/Province or Local status unrelated to the performance of the work involved.

jobs.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
President & Chief Executive Officer

The Will County Center for Economic Development (CED) seeks an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as its next President & Chief Executive Officer.
This is an opportunity to lead one of the Midwest's premier regional economic development organizations at a defining moment in its history. With a strong financial foundation, an experienced professional staff, engaged private-sector investors, and respected public-sector partnerships, the organization is well positioned for its next era of leadership.
Will County has emerged as one of the nation's most dynamic economic regions. Home to more than 700,000 residents, the county has led Illinois in job and population growth and become one of the country's premier logistics and advanced manufacturing markets. The CED leads regional initiatives in business attraction and retention, workforce development, housing, brownfield redevelopment, infrastructure advocacy, small business support, and long-range economic competitiveness.

The Organization

The Will County Center for Economic Development is a private, nonprofit economic development organization supported by a broad coalition of public and private investors. The organization serves as the county's lead economic development organization while working collaboratively across municipal boundaries and throughout the greater Chicagoland region.
The CED combines strategic leadership with practical execution. The organization also serves as a trusted convener, bringing together business, government, education, and community partners to advance projects that no single organization could accomplish alone.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will:
Provide strategic leadership for one of Illinois' leading regional economic development organizations.
Inspire and lead a talented professional staff while fostering a collaborative, innovative organizational culture.
Strengthen relationships with investors, municipalities, educational institutions, utilities, state agencies, and regional partners.
Advance initiatives that enhance the region's long-term economic competitiveness.
Ensure the long-term financial strength and sustainability of the organization through sound fiscal management and investor engagement.
Represent the organization with credibility and professionalism before business leaders, elected officials, community organizations, and the media.
Identify emerging economic trends and position the organization to capitalize on future opportunities.
Work closely with the Board of Directors to establish strategic priorities while ensuring excellence in organizational execution.

The Leadership Profile

The Board recognizes that exceptional economic development leadership can come from a variety of professional backgrounds. Candidates may have experience in economic development or related fields.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
A record of strategic leadership and organizational accomplishment. Demonstrated experience advancing economic development, community development, corporate expansion, real estate development, public-private partnerships, site selection, infrastructure, or related initiatives, with a record of successfully leading complex projects and bringing opportunities to completion.
Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills.
Strong financial and organizational management experience.
The ability to build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
Sound judgment, integrity, humility, and professionalism.
The ability to translate complex economic and organizational challenges into actionable strategies.
A collaborative leadership style that empowers staff while fostering accountability and high performance.
Educational requirements: Bachelor's Degree required in a relevant field such as business, economics, public administration from an accredited college or university. Advanced degree in a related field of study preferred.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Duties include but are not limited to the following:

Strategic Leadership and Management
·        Develop, in conjunction with the Board, annual and long-term strategic plans and provide timely reporting on accomplishments.
·        Shape an organizational culture for talent attraction and retention.
·        Provide executive level management, including the support and development of staff and oversight for performance management and adherence to human resource policies and practices.

Business Operations
·        Create strategies to promote the CED brand and Will County to investors and developers.
·        Develop and implement a comprehensive brand identity and marketing program to properly position Will County for business attraction, retention, and expansion efforts.
·        Work in collaboration with government agencies, business leaders, and other partners on strategies for advancing economic development.

Advocacy and External Engagement
·        Build and sustain effective working relationships with external stakeholders including but not limited to elected officials, business leaders, government agencies, and other partner organizations for purposes of driving economic development.
·        Act as the primary liaison between the local government agencies and other stakeholder groups and partners.
·        Serve as the chief spokesperson for the CED; a persuasive communicator of CED’s mission and services to current and potential partners, businesses, and other stakeholders.
·        Position CED as a highly regarded and trusted partner for advancing Will County’s economic development goals.
·        Serve on boards and attend events to advance the CED’s goals .

Financial Management and Oversight
·        Ensure that the CED maintains accurate financial records, including oversight for tax and audit services in conjunction with the Board and Finance Committee.
·        Develop annual plans and operating budgets for Board approval and ensure internal monitoring and compliance with annual budgets.
·        Oversee the preparation of financial reports and quarterly or monthly reporting to the Treasurer, Finance Committee, and Executive Committee as required by the Board.
·        Create and lead fundraising opportunities.
·        Safeguard the assts of the organization and ensure appropriate internal controls.

Board Relations
·        Serve as a non-voting member of the Board and as the principal liaison to the Board and committees.
·        Communicate effectively with the Board, providing timely and accurate information necessary for the Board to make informed decisions.
·        Develop, maintain, and support a strong Board and related committees.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be considered, as appropriate. 
·        Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in a related field, including but not limited to economics, business, or urban and regional planning.
·        Master’s degree preferred.
·        Significant and substantial portfolio of success in economic development, including executive experience with responsibility for strategy, staff, and budget.
·        Demonstrated experience leading economic development initiatives. 

Required Knowledge and Skills

·        Broad general knowledge of the leading economic development approaches and associated creative problem-solving techniques.
·        A deep understanding of the issues confronting Will County, and knowledge of best practices to confront those issues.
·        Demonstrated ability to support fundraising; and to identify and secure commitments from potential investors.
·        Exceptional organizational and strategic planning capability; experience managing public/private partnership initiatives is a plus.
·        Experience working with or reporting to a Board to advance strategic objectives.
·        Executive presence and political acumen with the requisite communication and influencing skills.

Compensation

Starting salary is between $170,000-$190,000 but will be commensurate with experience. This job includes a performance bonus based on individual and organizational goals.
Interested candidates should email a letter of interest and resume to jobs@willcountyced.com. Consideration of candidates will begin immediately and remain open until filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply early.

Brief Description

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the principal executive leader of Counseling & Recovery Services of Oklahoma (CRS) and is accountable to the Board of Directors for the overall strategic direction, organizational performance, financial sustainability, and community impact of the organization.

The CEO provides visionary, strategic, and transformational leadership, ensuring that all organizational activities are aligned with the mission, values, and long-term objectives established by the Board.

The CEO leads the organization in navigating a complex and evolving behavioral health environment, ensuring that CRS remains financially viable, operationally effective, technologically advanced, and highly responsive to the needs of the community.

This role requires a highly strategic, externally engaged, and operationally disciplined leader capable of guiding CRS through a complex and evolving landscape while maintaining strong financial health, advancing its mission, and delivering measurable community impact.

Duties And Responsibilities

Enterprise Leadership & Organizational Accountability

Provide enterprise leadership ensuring alignment of all organizational functions with Board-approved strategy and priorities.
Establish clear organizational goals, performance expectations, and accountability structures.
Ensure integration across clinical, operational, financial, and administrative functions.
Maintain appropriate delegation of authority while retaining accountability for outcomes.
Ensure the organization operates in a manner consistent with its mission, values, and service philosophy.

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Transformation

Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of the agency’s strategic plan.
Drive organizational transformation initiatives to improve effectiveness, scalability, and sustainability.
Establish and monitor enterprise-wide KPIs and performance dashboards to measure success and inform decision-making.
Ensure alignment of operational plans with long-term strategic priorities.
Evaluate and respond to emerging trends in behavioral health, nonprofit sustainability, reimbursement models, and public policy.
Promote a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and systems thinking.
Lead succession planning and leadership pipeline development to ensure organizational continuity.

Financial Leadership & Long-Term Sustainability

Partner with the Chief Financial Officer to develop annual operating budgets, multi-year financial forecasts, and long-term financial sustainability strategies.
Lead scenario planning to prepare for financial, regulatory, or market changes.
Oversee capital allocation and investment strategies to maximize organizational impact.
Monitor financial performance and key financial indicators, ensuring timely reporting to the Board.
Ensure appropriate internal controls, audits, and financial governance practices are in place.
Establish and oversee enterprise risk management frameworks across financial and operational areas.
Ensure compliance with all financial regulations, contracts, grants, and funding requirements.

Resource Development, Fundraising & External Engagement

Develop and lead a comprehensive fundraising and revenue diversification strategy.

Oversee optimization and utilization of electronic health records (EHR) and related systems.

Evaluate and appropriately leverage emerging technologies.

Executive Leadership, Talent & Organizational Culture

Establish and oversee leadership development and succession planning programs.
Ensure implementation of workforce planning strategies aligned with organizational needs.
Develop and lead initiatives to strengthen employee engagement, recruitment, retention, and organizational effectiveness.

Serve as steward of the organization’s culture, ensuring alignment with values and mission.

Program Oversight & Operational Excellence

Ensure programs align with strategic priorities and deliver measurable outcomes.
Monitor program performance through established KPIs and dashboards.
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and contractual obligations.
Ensure measurable standards for clinical quality, client outcomes, access to care, and service excellence are maintained.

Overall Position Purpose - Why

The Executive Director, Enterprise Solutions & Workforce Innovation provides executive leadership for Maryville University’s earned-revenue engine — workforce and corporate education, continuing and professional education, employer partnerships and credentialing, and consulting and professional services. As the counterpart to the Executive Director, Strategic Partnerships, this leader is accountable for building a scalable, self-sustaining, margin-positive business that diversifies the University’s revenue beyond tuition and philanthropy, deepens employer and industry relationships, expands non-traditional enrollment pathways, corporate educational partnerships and advances Maryville’s mission of community prosperity. The role partners closely with the University’s innovation and commercialization function to convert market-ready ideas and institutional assets into earned revenue. This is an entrepreneurial, P&L-accountable role for a builder who can grow both existing units and new lines of business.

Supervisory Responsibility

Provides executive leadership to MaryvilleWORKS (workforce, corporate & continuing education) and Maryville Solutions (consulting & professional services) leadership and teams, plus future enterprise-solutions staff. Serves as a peer to the Executive Director, Strategic Partnerships and the Founding Executive Director, Entrepreneurship & Innovation, who together own the division’s full revenue portfolio.

Essential Responsibilities - What You Will Be Doing

1

Strategic & business leadership.
Develop and execute the University’s earned-revenue and workforce strategy, translating market demand into a coherent, multi-year business plan; own the P&L for the earned-revenue lane, setting annual budgets, forecasts, pricing, and net-contribution goals and managing the business to them. Serve as a member of the IDCP leadership team and represent Maryville with business, government, philanthropic, and community organizations.

2

Corporate partnerships & business development.
Build and steward executive-level employer, corporate, and industry relationships that generate contracted, earned revenue; design, price, negotiate, and close customized workforce-education, training, and consulting agreements, including multi-year contracts, and educational partnerships, coordinating account strategy with the Executive Director, Strategic Partnerships so shared relationships are managed jointly.

3

MaryvilleWORKS — workforce, corporate & continuing education.
Lead and scale continuing education, certificates, industry certifications, MyMBA, and employer-sponsored and tuition-assistance education solutions; create stackable pathways from non-credit and professional programming into undergraduate and graduate degrees to grow non-traditional enrollment and net tuition.

4

Maryville Solutions — consulting & professional services.
Lead the growth of Maryville Solutions consulting services and build multidisciplinary, student-powered delivery teams that develop customized organizational, workforce, and technology solutions for employer and community clients, with disciplined scoping, pricing, and delivery.

5

Coordination with innovation & commercialization.
Partner with the Executive Director, Entrepreneurship & Innovation to bring market-ready programs, products, and services to employer and community customers, serving as the earned-revenue channel for commercializable assets with revenue attribution defined jointly so commercialization revenue is captured in the division’s earned-revenue portfolio.

6

Financial, operational & team leadership.
Deliver against explicit gross-revenue, net-revenue, and margin targets and report on the division’s cadence; oversee marketing, enrollment, CRM (Saints Outreach), technology, and operations for the lane; recruit, develop, and retain high-performing talent; and run the lane on the division’s operating system with clear roles, accountability, and traction.

Essential Qualifications

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability, and environmental conditions required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

It is also the responsibility of every employee of the University to remain current in their field, ensuring that they have the requisite knowledge and skills to perform the position at a high level. Requisite knowledge and skills change over time; therefore, the employee must be aware of changes and react to them by obtaining current knowledge and skills.

10+ years of progressively senior leadership in a revenue-generating business unit, with direct P&L ownership and a demonstrated record of building a self-sustaining, margin-positive enterprise.
Proven success in workforce development, corporate/continuing education, or a closely related earned-revenue business, including building and closing executive-level employer and industry partnerships.
Demonstrated business-development, contract-negotiation, financial-management, pricing, and forecasting skill.
Comfort operating in a base-plus-incentive, net-revenue-accountable structure and appetite for entrepreneurial, build-and-scale work.

DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT

The Organization:
The Georgia Historical Society (GHS) is the premier independent statewide institution responsible for collecting, examining, and teaching Georgia history. GHS houses the oldest and most distinguished collection of materials related exclusively to Georgia history in the nation. To learn more, go to www.georgiahistory.com

Job Summary:
The Director of Development is responsible for supporting the GHS mission and vision through acquisition of funding necessary to expand and sustain GHS programs. This person will maintain a high level of understanding of the GHS model and exhibit passion for the GHS mission and oversee development and implementation of annual and campaign-specific fundraising plans designed to obtain philanthropic gifts to advance the GHS research and educational mission. The Director of Development supports the efforts of the President/CEO, the Vice President/COO, the Board of Curators, key volunteers, and others to raise funds to meet specific measurable fundraising goals and monitor progress against those goals. Responsibilities will include creating and maintaining records and reports of development-related activities (e.g., campaign reports, donor reports). This role is responsible for formulating and supporting a funding strategy and for executing and/or overseeing the implementation of a development plan which deepens the commitment of existing donors, increases the number of overall supporters, and creates opportunities for all to contribute to GHS’s mission in practical and meaningful ways. The successful candidate will be energized by the opportunity to strengthen the existing development program and enhance the fundraising results of GHS. GHS boasts an influential, dynamic Board of Curators comprised of leaders from across the state of Georgia; the board is actively engaged in development efforts. This is a full-time, benefited, position located in Savannah, GA.

Job Duties and Responsibilities
(incumbent may perform other duties as assigned)

Development (Prospect Identification, Research, Relationship Management, and Solicitation)
Percentage of Role – 40%
Works with CEO and COO to develop, oversee, and implement a comprehensive annual fundraising plan inclusive of board, corporate, foundation, individual donor, and membership giving as well as development events. Oversees annual and ongoing campaigns, to include the Annual Appeal, Georgia History Festival , Endowment, and Planned Giving campaigns. This includes working with others to coordinate efforts of the CEO, COO, board members, and volunteers to solicit donations by researching, analyzing, and identifying major corporate, foundation, and individual donors, and assists with developing solicitation proposals and talking points for the CEO, board members, and other leadership as needed. Works with the senior leadership team to identify funds needed and preferred funding targets and approaches. Identifies and cultivates major gift prospects, as well as corporate and foundation donors. President & Chief Executive Officer

The Will County Center for Economic Development (CED) seeks an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as its next President & Chief Executive Officer.
This is an opportunity to lead one of the Midwest's premier regional economic development organizations at a defining moment in its history. With a strong financial foundation, an experienced professional staff, engaged private-sector investors, and respected public-sector partnerships, the organization is well positioned for its next era of leadership.
Will County has emerged as one of the nation's most dynamic economic regions. Home to more than 700,000 residents, the county has led Illinois in job and population growth and become one of the country's premier logistics and advanced manufacturing markets. The CED leads regional initiatives in business attraction and retention, workforce development, housing, brownfield redevelopment, infrastructure advocacy, small business support, and long-range economic competitiveness.

The Organization

The Will County Center for Economic Development is a private, nonprofit economic development organization supported by a broad coalition of public and private investors. The organization serves as the county's lead economic development organization while working collaboratively across municipal boundaries and throughout the greater Chicagoland region.
The CED combines strategic leadership with practical execution. The organization also serves as a trusted convener, bringing together business, government, education, and community partners to advance projects that no single organization could accomplish alone.

What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will:
Provide strategic leadership for one of Illinois' leading regional economic development organizations.
Inspire and lead a talented professional staff while fostering a collaborative, innovative organizational culture.
Strengthen relationships with investors, municipalities, educational institutions, utilities, state agencies, and regional partners.
Advance initiatives that enhance the region's long-term economic competitiveness.
Ensure the long-term financial strength and sustainability of the organization through sound fiscal management and investor engagement.
Represent the organization with credibility and professionalism before business leaders, elected officials, community organizations, and the media.
Identify emerging economic trends and position the organization to capitalize on future opportunities.
Work closely with the Board of Directors to establish strategic priorities while ensuring excellence in organizational execution.

The Leadership Profile

The Board recognizes that exceptional economic development leadership can come from a variety of professional backgrounds. Candidates may have experience in economic development or related fields.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
A record of strategic leadership and organizational accomplishment. Demonstrated experience advancing economic development, community development, corporate expansion, real estate development, public-private partnerships, site selection, infrastructure, or related initiatives, with a record of successfully leading complex projects and bringing opportunities to completion.
Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills.
Strong financial and organizational management experience.
The ability to build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
Sound judgment, integrity, humility, and professionalism.
The ability to translate complex economic and organizational challenges into actionable strategies.
A collaborative leadership style that empowers staff while fostering accountability and high performance.
Educational requirements: Bachelor's Degree required in a relevant field such as business, economics, public administration from an accredited college or university. Advanced degree in a related field of study preferred.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Duties include but are not limited to the following:

Strategic Leadership and Management
·        Develop, in conjunction with the Board, annual and long-term strategic plans and provide timely reporting on accomplishments.
·        Shape an organizational culture for talent attraction and retention.
·        Provide executive level management, including the support and development of staff and oversight for performance management and adherence to human resource policies and practices.

Business Operations
·        Create strategies to promote the CED brand and Will County to investors and developers.
·        Develop and implement a comprehensive brand identity and marketing program to properly position Will County for business attraction, retention, and expansion efforts.
·        Work in collaboration with government agencies, business leaders, and other partners on strategies for advancing economic development.

Advocacy and External Engagement
·        Build and sustain effective working relationships with external stakeholders including but not limited to elected officials, business leaders, government agencies, and other partner organizations for purposes of driving economic development.
·        Act as the primary liaison between the local government agencies and other stakeholder groups and partners.
·        Serve as the chief spokesperson for the CED; a persuasive communicator of CED’s mission and services to current and potential partners, businesses, and other stakeholders.
·        Position CED as a highly regarded and trusted partner for advancing Will County’s economic development goals.
·        Serve on boards and attend events to advance the CED’s goals .

Financial Management and Oversight
·        Ensure that the CED maintains accurate financial records, including oversight for tax and audit services in conjunction with the Board and Finance Committee.
·        Develop annual plans and operating budgets for Board approval and ensure internal monitoring and compliance with annual budgets.
·        Oversee the preparation of financial reports and quarterly or monthly reporting to the Treasurer, Finance Committee, and Executive Committee as required by the Board.
·        Create and lead fundraising opportunities.
·        Safeguard the assts of the organization and ensure appropriate internal controls.

·        A deep understanding of the issues confronting Will County, and knowledge of best practices to confront those issues.

The successful candidate will be energized by the opportunity to strengthen the existing development program and enhance the fundraising results of GHS. GHS boasts an influential, dynamic Board of Curators comprised of leaders from across the state of Georgia; the board is actively engaged in development efforts. Development (Prospect Identification, Research, Relationship Management, and Solicitation)
Percentage of Role – 40%

Oversees annual and ongoing campaigns, to include the Annual Appeal, Georgia History Festival , Endowment, and Planned Giving campaigns. new_jobs.description:
Uniquity Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to putting science and patients first. We exist to develop transformative new medicines for immune-mediated diseases, and we’re looking for bright-minded professionals driven by a desire to advance science and make a difference for people in need. Our lead asset, solrikitug, is a highly potent TSLP inhibitor now in Phase 2 clinical trials for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) indications.

Join us in building an organization where people and science thrive together. You’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while working alongside a talented, agile team in an environment where ideas move quickly, colleagues are trusted, and quality remains a cornerstone.

The Executive Director, Clinical Operations –provides strategic and operational leadership for the planning, execution, and oversight of global Phase 1–3 clinical trials across Uniquity Bio’s respiratory development programs. This role is responsible for ensuring studies are delivered with operational excellence, quality, speed, scientific rigor, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

The Executive Director will lead high-performing clinical operations teams and serve as a key cross-functional partner to Clinical Development, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Supply, Clinical Quality, Medical Writing, and external CROs/vendors to advance programs from early development through pivotal-stage execution.

The ideal candidate is an experienced clinical operations leader who thrives in a fast-paced biotech environment, excels at solving complex operational challenges, and can effectively balance strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Program Leadership & Execution

Develop and execute Clinical Operations strategies aligned with corporate objectives and the clinical development portfolio
Provide strategic operational leadership for clinical programs from study start-up through database lock and study closeout
Lead execution of global Phase 1–3 clinical trials, ensuring delivery against timelines, budgets, quality standards, and regulatory requirements
Drive operational strategy and execution planning across multiple studies and programs
Proactively identify operational risks develop mitigation strategies, and lead resolution of critical issues.
Contribute operational expertise to clinical development plans, protocol development, feasibility assessments, enrollment strategies, and go/no-go decision-making
Ensure studies are conducted in accordance with protocols, ICH-GCP, SOPs, and applicable global regulatory requirements
Monitor study timelines, enrollment performance, operational metrics, and quality indicators to ensure successful delivery
Provide escalation management and proactive problem-solving for operational challenges
Develop and execute the Clinical Operations strategy aligned with corporate and development objectives
Ensure consistent application of operational best practices across the clinical portfolio

Study Team & Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner closely with Clinical Development, Biometrics, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Quality, Clinical Supply, Medical Writing, and other functions to support integrated program execution
Facilitate governance discussions and communicate study status, risks, mitigation strategies, and key operational updates to senior leadership
Partner with senior leadership on portfolio planning, prioritization, resource forecasting, and budgeting
Participate in development team meetings, governance committees, and executive-level updates
Support due diligence activities, business development initiatives, and strategic partnerships as needed

CRO & Vendor Oversight

Lead CRO and vendor selection, onboarding, governance and performance management activities
Establish clear operational expectations, KPIs and accountability measures across external partners
Ensure vendor deliverables, study metrics, timeline, and quality standards are consistently achieved
Review vendor performance, deliverables and study metrics to ensure quality and execution standards are met
Drive effective collaboration across CROs, central laboratories, and specialty vendors while maintaining appropriate sponsor oversight

Financial & Resource Management

Lead development and ongoing management of clinical operations budgets and forecasts
Monitor financial performance, identify variances, and implement appropriate cost management strategies
Develop portfolio-level resource and capacity plans aligned with current and future clinical development needs
Ensure effective utilization of internal resources, CROs, vendors, and other external partners
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and optimize clinical development costs without compromising quality

Operational Excellence & Infrastructure

Drive operational excellence, process optimization, and continuous improvement initiatives across Clinical Operations
Support the development and refinement of SOPs, processes, tools, and scalable operational infrastructure to support pipeline growth
Ensure inspection readiness across studies and programs at all times
Support internal audits, regulatory inspections, CAPA activities, and quality-focused operational execution
Maintain compliance with company policies, SOPs, GCP, ICH guidelines, FDA regulations, and applicable global regulatory standards
Identify and implement innovative approaches and technologies that enhance clinical trial execution
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, quality, and continuous improvement

Team Leadership & Development

Build, mentor, and develop high-performing Clinical Operations teams within a collaborative and growth-oriented environment
Foster a culture of accountability, transparency, urgency, teamwork, and operational excellence
Establish performance objectives and support career development planning for team members
Help shape organizational structure and operational support models as the Clinical Operations function evolves
Serve as a trusted operational leader within the Development organization

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced scientific or healthcare degree preferred
15+ years of biotech/pharmaceutical clinical operations experience with increasing leadership responsibility
Significant experience leading Phase 1–3 global clinical trials within respiratory, pulmonary or inflammatory disease programs strongly preferred
Demonstrated success managing complex clinical programs within lean biotech or fast-growth environments
Strong experience overseeing CROs, vendors and external partnerships
Deep understanding of ICH-GCP, FDA regulations and clinical trial operational requirements
Prior people management and organizational leadership experience strongly preferred

Required Knowledge, Skills, Abilities & Behaviors

Strong strategic and operational leadership capabilities
Exceptional project management and organizational skills
Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
Strong executive presence and ability to influence across teams and levels
Proactive, solutions-oriented and execution-focused mindset
Ability to manage complexity while maintaining attention to detail
Comfortable balancing strategic planning with hands-on operational execution
Strong judgment, prioritization and decision-making capabilities

Work Environment

At Uniquity Bio, we believe every team member has an impact on the patients we aim to serve. We are a nimble team with a rigorous approach to drug development that requires collaboration and transparency to maximize value, reduce risk, and deliver meaningful, best-in-class products. We are looking for self-starters who enjoy working in a complex, collaborative environment and are motivated to bring critical new medicines to people around the world. We are a small, fast-paced organization with a talented team of in-house employees and external consultants. Candidates must be self-motivated and able to work both independently and collaboratively to achieve success and impact in our dynamic work environment.

This is a U.S.-based position. Team members who live within commuting distance of our Malvern, PA or San Diego, CA office locations are expected to spend time in the office, and remote employees are expected to travel to an office on a regular basis. Specific details for both local and remote staff will be discussed and agreed upon on a case-by-case basis with the employee’s manager. Business travel may be required depending upon the specific needs of the position.

The above job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Requirements of the position may change from time to time based on business needs.

Uniquity Bio is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

new_jobs.title: Vocational Program Director
new_jobs.description:
Nexus Neurorecovery Center | Conroe, Texas

Lead a nationally recognized vocational rehabilitation program and help individuals rebuild their lives after brain injury.

At Nexus Neurorecovery Center (NNC)
, we believe recovery extends beyond the hospital—it means helping individuals regain independence, purpose, and meaningful employment. As part of Nexus Health Systems
, our 26-acre neurorehabilitation campus in Conroe provides comprehensive inpatient, residential, outpatient, and vocational rehabilitation services for adults recovering from traumatic brain injury (TBI), stroke, spinal cord injury (SCI), and other complex neurological conditions.

Supported by an exceptional interdisciplinary team of physicians, therapists, psychologists, nurses, and rehabilitation specialists, NNC proudly holds five CARF Three-Year Accreditations
, including Brain Injury Specialty Program – Vocational Services
. Our collaborative approach combines medical, behavioral, and rehabilitative care to help patients achieve greater independence and successful community reintegration.

We're looking for an experienced Vocational Program Director
to lead, grow, and elevate our CARF-accredited vocational rehabilitation program while helping patients transition from recovery to meaningful employment and independent living.

Why Join Nexus?

This is more than a leadership position—it's an opportunity to shape one of Texas' premier vocational rehabilitation programs.

You'll have the support of executive leadership, a collaborative interdisciplinary team, and the resources needed to build innovative programming that changes lives.

What We Offer

Comprehensive Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid Time Off
Continuing education and certification support
Relocation assistance available
Collaborative, mission-driven culture
Opportunity to lead one of the region's most respected neurorehabilitation vocational programs

What You'll Do
Lead the Vocational Rehabilitation Program

Provide strategic and clinical leadership for NNC's CARF-accredited Vocational Services Program.
Drive continuous program improvement while maintaining the highest standards of clinical quality and patient outcomes.
Oversee departmental operations, budgeting, performance metrics, and accreditation readiness.
Develop innovative vocational programming that prepares individuals with acquired brain injuries and neurological conditions for successful community employment.

Collaborate with the Interdisciplinary Team

Serve as an active member of the interdisciplinary treatment team.
Partner with physicians, nursing, behavioral health, and rehabilitation therapists to integrate vocational goals into individualized treatment plans.
Ensure vocational rehabilitation is incorporated early in the recovery process and remains a core component of patient care.

Build Community & Employer Partnerships

Develop relationships with employers throughout the Greater Houston and Conroe communities.
Expand competitive employment opportunities through strategic partnerships.
Collaborate with Texas Workforce Commission Vocational Rehabilitation (TWC-VR) and other community organizations.
Promote community integration and long-term employment success for patients.

Lead and Develop Your Team

Recruit, mentor, supervise, and develop vocational rehabilitation professionals.
Foster a culture centered on evidence-based practice, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Provide leadership that supports professional growth and exceptional patient care.

Drive Results

Monitor patient outcomes and program performance using meaningful data and quality metrics.
Maintain CARF accreditation standards and ensure regulatory compliance.
Identify opportunities to enhance services, improve patient outcomes, and expand vocational programming.

Qualifications
Required

Master's degree in Rehabilitation Counseling, Vocational Rehabilitation, or a closely related field
Current Certified Rehabilitation Counselor (CRC) credential
Minimum 7 years of vocational rehabilitation experience serving individuals with acquired brain injury or other neurological conditions
Minimum 3 years of leadership or program management experience
Experience working in inpatient, post-acute rehabilitation, behavioral health, or neurorehabilitation settings
Knowledge of CARF accreditation standards and quality improvement processes
Excellent leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills

Preferred

Certified Brain Injury Specialist (CBIS) or Certified Brain Injury Specialist Trainer (CBIST)
Experience with Individual Placement and Support (IPS) or other evidence-based supported employment models
Experience working with Texas Workforce Commission Vocational Rehabilitation (TWC-VR)
Certified Work Incentives Counselor (CWIC) or knowledge of SSI/SSDI work incentives
Experience building employer partnerships and community employment networks

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a collaborative leader who understands that successful vocational rehabilitation is about more than helping someone find a job—it's about restoring confidence, independence, and purpose.

You'll be comfortable collaborating with physicians and therapists during treatment planning, mentoring staff, developing employer partnerships, analyzing program outcomes, and advocating for patients throughout their recovery journey. Most importantly, you'll be passionate about helping individuals with neurological injuries and disabilities achieve meaningful, productive lives.

Make an Impact

Every patient has a story, a goal, and the potential to achieve meaningful independence. As Vocational Program Director
, you'll help transform recovery into opportunity by creating pathways back to work, community, and purpose.

If you're ready to lead an established program while helping shape the future of neurorehabilitation, we invite you to join the team at Nexus Neurorecovery Center
.

Apply today and help patients reclaim independence through meaningful employment and community reintegration
